prompt: Why is a JSON log line easier for a program than a sentence?

choices.text: Each value has a name, so a query asks for the field
choices.why: Right. No regular expression has to know where a number sits.

choices.text: It is shorter, so it is faster to read from disk
choices.why: The JSON line is longer.

choices.text: JSON is compressed and sentences are not
choices.why: Neither is compressed by being JSON.

choices.text: Log collectors refuse lines that are not JSON
choices.why: They accept any text.

prompt: Of the 2000 made-up checkouts, how many took 150 ms or more?
The regular expression found the same 49 as `jq`. Why is it still the worse tool?
hint: What happens when the sentence changes?

choices.text: It is slower on two thousand lines
choices.why: Speed is not the problem at this size.

choices.text: It breaks when the sentence's wording or units change
choices.why: Right, and it is hard to read and to extend.

choices.text: `grep` cannot count matches
choices.why: `grep -c` counted them.

choices.text: It found the right lines by luck
choices.why: It was correct, for this wording.

prompt: Why does the storefront log the fixed message "checkout finished" and put the order number in a field?

choices.text: Fixed messages are translated automatically
choices.why: Nothing translates them.

choices.text: So events are counted by message and searched by field
choices.why: Right. An interpolated message is a different string every time.

choices.text: Numbers are not allowed inside a message
choices.why: They are allowed; they just make it uncountable.

choices.text: The order number is personal data
choices.why: An order number identifies an order, not a person, and it is logged anyway.

prompt: Where do the shop's services write their logs?

choices.text: To a file per service, rotated daily
choices.why: Files are what the shop avoids.

choices.text: Straight to Loki over HTTP
choices.why: The service knows nothing about Loki.

choices.text: To standard output
choices.why: Right: whatever runs the service collects it.

choices.text: To the Collector, through the OpenTelemetry SDK
choices.why: In this lab logs leave through stdout and Docker.

prompt: Match each part of the formatter to what it gives every line.
With `LOG_LEVEL=INFO`, which of DEBUG, INFO, WARNING and ERROR are written?

choices.text: Only INFO
choices.why: Everything above the floor is written too.

choices.text: All four
choices.why: DEBUG is below the floor.

choices.text: INFO, WARNING and ERROR
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: DEBUG and INFO
choices.why: The level is a floor, not a ceiling.

prompt: A card is declined. At which level should the storefront log it?

choices.text: INFO
choices.why: Right: a normal outcome, not a failure of the service.

choices.text: ERROR, because the customer could not pay
choices.why: The service worked; declining was its job.

choices.text: CRITICAL, because money is involved
choices.why: Money does not make a normal outcome critical.

choices.text: WARNING, in case it happens often
choices.why: A rate is a metric's job, not a level's.

prompt: Payments is misbehaving and you want its DEBUG lines for ten minutes. What lets you do it without a new release?
hint: The three runs changed nothing in the code.

choices.text: Editing the formatter to print everything
choices.why: That is a code change.

choices.text: Restarting it with `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`
choices.why: Right, and back afterwards.

choices.text: Asking Loki to keep DEBUG lines
choices.why: Lines below the level are never written.

choices.text: Raising Prometheus's scrape rate
choices.why: Logs are not scraped.

prompt: Which of these field habits cause queries to silently miss lines? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `order_id` in one service and `orderId` in another
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: `duration` in seconds here and milliseconds there
choices.why: Yes: off by a thousand.

choices.text: `trace_id` in every service
choices.why: That is the consistency that helps.

choices.text: `order_id` sometimes a number and sometimes `"none"`
choices.why: Yes: an indexing backend refuses or drops the lines that disagree.

prompt: The shop puts the unit in the field's name, as in `duration____`.
How did lesson 1's Loki query find the payments lines by `service_name`, when the shop only writes `service`?
hint: Something sits between stdout and Loki.

choices.text: Loki guesses the service from the container's name
choices.why: It received the name from the pipeline.

choices.text: The formatter writes both names
choices.why: It writes only `service`.

choices.text: The Collector copied `service` into the resource
choices.why: Right, mapping the JSON into OpenTelemetry's log model.

choices.text: Grafana renames the label when it draws
choices.why: The query went to Loki directly.

prompt: Which lines in the shop have no `trace_id`?
hint: When no request is being handled.

choices.text: Every ERROR line
choices.why: Errors inside a request carry it.

choices.text: Start-up lines
choices.why: Right: no span is current then.

choices.text: Every line from orders, which has no tracing code
choices.why: orders is traced automatically, and its lines carry the id.

choices.text: Lines longer than 245 bytes
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Why take the id from tracing rather than generate a `request_id` of the shop's own?
hint: What would the home-made one need?

choices.text: A request id cannot be put in JSON
choices.why: It can.

choices.text: Trace ids are shorter
choices.why: They are 32 hex digits.

choices.text: It is already propagated, with no extra plumbing
choices.why: Right: a home-made one needs its own header, reading and passing.

choices.text: Loki only indexes trace ids
choices.why: That is not why.

prompt: The uncaught traceback printed 17 lines. How many records does a line-by-line log pipeline store?

choices.text: One, because Python marks the traceback as one event
choices.why: Plain text carries no such mark.
Right, and they can be separated.

choices.text: None: stderr is not collected
choices.why: Docker collects both streams.

choices.text: Two: the first and the last
choices.why: Every line is kept.

prompt: What did `log.exception` produce through the shop's formatter?

choices.text: Seventeen JSON lines, one per traceback line
choices.why: It produced one.

choices.text: One line, with the traceback dropped to save space
choices.why: The traceback is there, in a field.

choices.text: One line, with the traceback in a field
choices.why: Right, never split from its message.

choices.text: Nothing, because the exception was caught
choices.why: Catching is where it is logged.

prompt: A database error is logged by the repository, again by the service layer and again by the handler. What does the error count show?
hint: Log once, where it is handled.

choices.text: Three errors for one failure
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: One error, because the trace id is the same
choices.why: Counts are of lines, and there are three.

choices.text: Zero, because rethrown errors are ignored
choices.why: Nothing ignores them.

choices.text: An exact count, since each layer adds detail
choices.why: Detail is fine; the triple count is not.

prompt: The four services wrote 260212 bytes in one minute. Roughly how many megabytes is that per day? Answer to the nearest ten.
hint: 1440 minutes, a million bytes per MB.

prompt: Which is the first answer to log volume, before sampling?

choices.text: Compress the lines in the service
choices.why: Compression is the backend's job, and saves storage, not reading.

choices.text: Stop writing lines nobody reads
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Keep one ERROR line in ten
choices.why: Errors are never sampled.

choices.text: Shorten every field name to two letters
choices.why: That destroys the interface for a few bytes.

prompt: The sampled run kept 95 of 990 INFO lines. What can it no longer answer?

choices.text: Roughly how often checkouts finish
choices.why: A sample still estimates that.

choices.text: Whether any warnings happened
choices.why: All 10 were kept.

choices.text: What happened to one particular order
choices.why: Right: its line was probably dropped.

choices.text: What the messages look like
choices.why: Any kept line shows that.
